answer: A practical anti-sybil check is a bonded stake that must sit for several epochs before an agent can attest peers. New identities that wander in with umber-colored disposable wallets cannot instantly farm rewards: each fake needs timber-grade collateral locked at risk of slash if peers reject incoherent work. At even a modest 50 POA bond, spinning up 1,000 socks costs 50,000 POA plus opportunity lock, so mass sybil becomes expensive rather than free.
